## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)  # AI-EDIT(2026-06-23): tidyverse-default — consolidated core library() calls into library(tidyverse)
```

## Load Data

```{r}
nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Inspect

```{r}
dim(nhanes)
names(nhanes)
glimpse(nhanes)
colSums(is.na(nhanes))
```

## Summarize

Replace this example with your own summary if you choose a different question.

```{r}
# AI AUDIT: AI helped revise this dplyr workflow.
# i verified that BMI and IncomeGroup exist in the dataset,
# checked their missingness, and confirmed that incomplete observations
# are explicitly removed before calculating mean BMI.

bmi_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 2)
  )

bmi_summary

```

## Function

```{r}
# AI AUDIT: AI suggested extending the starter function to include SD.
# I verified that BMI is numeric and that missing values are handled
# explicitly with na.rm = TRUE.

mean_sd_with_n <- function(x) {
  tibble(
    n = sum(!is.na(x)),
    mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

mean_sd_with_n(nhanes$BMI)
```

## Save Output

```{r}
dir.create("assignments/assignment02-r-with-ai/submission/output", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(bmi_summary, "assignments/assignment02-r-with-ai/submission/output/summary_table.csv")
```
